trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Lost money: -72.69% total return vs +14.41% for the index, -79.63pp residual after beta, -73.5% max drawdown, 1.25% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at -72.69% - a 72,690 dollar loss on 100,000 of starting capital, in a market that returned +14.41%.
The momentum premium it is built to harvest was live (+4.98%) and the account STILL lost 72.69% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
The reversal premium it is built to harvest went the wrong way (+19.00% over the season), so the signal was fighting the tape and the account lost 72.69%.
The beta premium it is built to harvest was live (+39.71%) and the account STILL lost 72.69% - so the loss came from implementation, timing or leverage, not from a missing signal.
The liquidity premium it is built to harvest went the wrong way (+0.83% over the season), so the signal was fighting the tape and the account lost 72.69%.
Of the -72.69% total, about +6.94pp is explained by carrying beta 0.48 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.06); the residual -79.63pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
XOM contributed +1,032 USD across 2 closed trades; CVNA was the biggest drag at -29,480 USD.
Execution cost 1,247 USD (1.25% of starting capital, 1.5 bp per fill, 1.6 bp of the 7,800,692 USD traded). 75% of that was spread/depth/impact and 25% was explicit fees and rebates.
194 closed round trips, 35.1% winners, profit factor 0.29, average winner +440 vs average loser -814 USD, median holding 1 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 248 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 1944 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: CVNA long 2025-10-23 to 2025-10-24, -4,279 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -73.48% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-09-14, never recovered. Average gross exposure 16% of starting capital, peak leverage 1.61x.
Daily returns were -1.55 skewed with excess kurtosis +4.89; historical 95% VaR -3.27%/day with CVaR -5.04%/day. Worst single session -8.13%, best +4.03%.
Standing limitations of this simulation that apply to this participant regardless of the regime: Cannot see intraday volume at decision time in a daily-bar simulation (flagged limitation)

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Gap-and-fade days: the open print is the high of day.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 75.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @GapAndGo_YOLO (Gap And Go) ran the "intraday momentum" archetype. Declared thesis: A stock that gaps up on the open has absorbed news or imbalanced overnight order flow; continuation in the first hours is common because retail and institutional demand arrives through the session. Take the continuation and be flat before the close so nothing is held overnight. Entry: At the open, compute gap = open / prior close - 1; Buy any name gapping up more than +1.5%; Skip names whose quoted spread is wider than 30 bp (costs eat the edge). Exit: Exit every position at the same session's close (market-on-close order); No stop loss intraday. Sizing: equal 40% of equity across qualifying names, capped at 4 names = up to 160% gross. Leverage: up to 1.6x gross. Cadence: daily, horizon intraday. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Turns the whole account over every day, so a small per-trade edge compounds ~250 times a year.
